title: Revisiting Jiahu’s 9000-Year-Old Fermented Beverage: New Microfossil Evidence for Early Qu-Based and Malt-Based Brewing Technologies in North China
lineage: Publisher’s original open-access PDF. Supplement PDF extracted from publisher ZIP https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/heritage/heritage-09-00335/article_deploy/heritage-09-00335-s001.zip (ZIP SHA-256 aa664f5aed29cdcde7f534b549704d297a02efef8e2d9c9e2c5e2fca8ea938a0). Juzhong Zhang also coauthored the 2004 study. Different assays, a shared find context and unverified overlap of individual sherds.

passages.note: Liu and colleagues describe damaged starch, rice and abundant Monascus-like remains in jar and bottle interiors. They infer qu-like saccharification and some possible malt processing. The molecular evidence for honey and fruit is weaker, though these ingredients remain possible.

The newer sampling context identifiers include POT8 from ash pit T14H32. The 2004 paper’s note 10 lists T14/H32, confirming common context nomenclature without uniquely identifying the same physical fragment.
